applies_to: EVAPCO eco-Air air-cooled and adiabatic fluid coolers, CO2 gas coolers and condensers with EC fan motors.
summary: The eco-Air PLC panel exposes BACnet IP on its Ethernet port and BACnet MS/TP on a shared RS-485 terminal that can run either MS/TP or Modbus RTU, chosen on the HMI. Objects are plain Binary and Analog Values numbered from 0, covering unit enable and state, process and ambient temperature, setpoints, fan-speed limits, adiabatic pre-cooling stages and per-fan EC motor alarms, speeds and communication status.
notes: Per-fan objects (EC fan alarm and communication status, speed feedback) only matter for the number of fans fitted.
BV 13-76 and AV 49-100 are EC-fan objects; AC/NEMA-motor units use a separate edition of the guide.
Units column 'Deg.' follows the unit's configured temperature scale.
The guide prints the same object name (bnWarnBits_EBM_01) for all twenty AV 49-68 (fans 1-20); names are kept as printed, so check the live object names.

source.title: EVAPCO Controller User's Manual Addendum - Communications Guide EC Motor Edition

integration.summary: Pick MS/TP or Modbus RTU for the serial port on the HMI (BACnet IP is always live on Ethernet), set the addresses under Service > BMS & Network, then enable the unit through BV 0 if it is configured for BMS enable. Monitor AV 16 unit state, AV 0 outlet temperature and the common alarm, and write AV 3 for the process setpoint. For BMS fan-speed control enable BV 77, set AV 101 to Communication and write AV 105.

integration.enable: Write BV 0 bnEnableUnit = 1; it only takes effect when the unit is configured to be enabled via BMS. AV 16 reports 4 when the unit is off via BMS.
integration.remote_sensors: Fan speed can be driven remotely: set BV 77 bnRemoteEnable = 1, AV 101 bnRemoteSource = 2 (Communication) and write AV 105 bnRemoteFanSpeed. AV 103/AV 104 are fallback high/low speeds used when the analog speed input is lost, chosen by ambient against AV 102.
setup: Default communication parameters are printed on page 1 of the panel wiring diagram, not in this guide.
Change BACnet/Modbus settings with the unit switched off: log in at Service level, Service > BMS & Network, then hold Update for 3 s (HMI and PLC restart).
The RS-485 port runs either BACnet MS/TP or Modbus RTU, never both; BACnet IP and Modbus TCP share the Ethernet port and both stay active.
gotchas: Writable parameters are stored in the PLC's non-volatile memory, rated for about 100,000 writes; never write them cyclically.
Points marked for adiabatic units (pre-cooling valves, flush, wet-stage timers) can be ignored on dry-only units.
Per-fan point blocks repeat for each EC fan; unused fan numbers will read normal/offline.
